## Technical Analysis

**[10]** Huang, Ken. "Chapter 15: Structured Output and Schema-Constrained Generation (Claude Code vs. Hermes Agent)." *Substack*, May 2, 2026.

## Benchmarks and Research

**[13]** "JSONSchemaBench: Real-World Schema Complexity Breaks LLM Structured Output Guarantees." *Bean Labs Research*, July 8, 2026.
<https://beancount.io/bean-labs/research-logs/2026/07/08/jsonschemabench-structured-outputs-language-models>
**Tier:** 2
9,558 real-world schemas benchmark. Complex schemas (GitHub-Hard): Guidance 41%, OpenAI 9%, Outlines 3%, Gemini 0%. XGrammar: 38 under-constrained failures. JSON Schema feature support: max 13/45 (Guidance).
Note: Does not include Claude/Anthropic data.

**[14]** "Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models." *arXiv*, 2024.
<https://arxiv.org/html/2403.06988v1>
**Tier:** 1
Demonstrates constrained decoding reduces reasoning accuracy by up to 11 percentage points on GSM8K (Llama-2 13B: 26.2% → 15.2%). NER accuracy more than halved (Mistral 7B: 21.0% → 9.8%). Proposes minimally invasive "Domino" approach that preserves accuracy.

**[15]** "LLM Structured Output Benchmarks are Riddled with Mistakes." *Cleanlab Blog*, 2026.
<https://cleanlab.ai/blog/structured-output-benchmark/>
**Tier:** 2
Found errors in every public structured output benchmark examined. Best model-task output accuracy: 77% (Gemini 3 Pro on Data Table Analysis). Insurance claims: all models failed 60-70% of the time.

**[16]** "LLM Structured Output: Schemas, Retries, Constrained Decoding." *Easton Dev Blog*, May 6, 2026.
<https://eastondev.com/blog/en/posts/ai/20260506-llm-structured-output/>
**Tier:** 3
Three-layer reliability architecture. Failure rates: prompt-only 5-10%, JSON Mode 2-5%, Strict <0.1%, Outlines FSM 0%. Temperature 0.7 → 15% format errors vs 0.1 near-zero. Claude strict parameter quote: "currently ignored for tool definitions."
